# The Cognitive Brain {#sec-brain}

::: {.column-margin}

\chapterminitoc

:::

![*Systems organ focus: The brain.* The four-tier physical AI systems architecture highlights the cognitive deliberative layer. Operating above the real-time nervous system and physical body, the learned brain processes high-dimensional multimodal streams to generate candidate proposals, with execution authority reserved for downstream deterministic safety governors.](figures/fig_locator.svg){#fig-locator fig-pos="H" width=100%}

Every embodied agent requires a cognitive core—a brain that perceives physical reality, maintains spatial memory, and synthesizes candidate motion trajectories. In classical robotics, this layer was authored through explicit differential equations and state machines, which break down in unstructured environments. Physical AI introduces high-capacity foundation models to generalize across open worlds. Yet this statistical power introduces critical vulnerabilities: neural models forfeit formal verifiability, output uncalibrated confidence, and collide with the physical Memory Wall during real-time weight streaming. To engineer dependable machines, we must treat the learned brain as an unprivileged proposal engine—harnessing its generalizability while delegating all execution authority to deterministic safety governors.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-objective}
After studying this chapter, you will be able to:

1. Identify the five ideal properties required of an embodied cognitive brain and trace its role in the four-tier physical AI stack.
2. Explain the historical and practical motivations behind the shift from classical analytical models to learned representations in physical systems.
3. Contrast classical analytical methods with learned foundation models across generalizability, sensory robustness, and formal mathematical verifiability.
4. Trace the five foundational stages of the learned cognitive pipeline: Ingestion, Perception, Memory, Intent, and Planning.
5. Ground each cognitive stage in physical robot archetypes (mobile systems, manipulators, process plants) and evaluate their systems engineering implications.
6. Diagnose the four core cognitive failure modes: semantic hallucinations, out-of-distribution overconfidence, perceptual chattering, and temporal expiration.
7. Apply the Proposal–Permission Principle and Two-Speed Brain architecture to decouple statistical deliberation from real-time safety enforcement.

*Core chapter takeaway.* Learned models provide open-world generalizability and sensory robustness that classical equations cannot achieve, but they lack formal safety guarantees. In physical AI, the brain earns the capability to propose what the machine might attempt, but never the authority to grant permission for physical action.
:::

## The Embodied Brain {#sec-brain-3-1}

<!-- SECTION 3.1 -->
<!-- claim: An embodied brain governs the deliberative cognitive layer and must satisfy five ideal properties that distinguish it from disembodied intelligence. -->
<!-- covers: Reference the cover organ locator image (#fig-locator) to set up the whole architectural stack. -->
<!-- covers: Embodied AI vs Disembodied LLMs: tokens vs moving mass, reversible queries vs irreversible kinetic energy. -->
<!-- covers: Five Ideal Properties: 1. Semantic Generalizability, 2. Continuous Sensory Robustness, 3. Metric Spatial-Temporal Grounding, 4. Multi-Rate Cadence Decoupling, 5. Bounded Execution Authority. -->
<!-- covers: Progressive disclosure: build from simple intuition to foundational systems properties. -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
\lettrine{A}{s} highlighted in the systems organ locator at the opening of this chapter (@fig-locator), the brain occupies the topmost deliberative tier in the physical AI architecture. In @sec-boundary, we established that physical AI begins the instant digital computation crosses the causal boundary to command physical mass, while @sec-body quantified the unyielding budgets of freshness, stopping distance, reflected inertia, and thermal dissipation that govern the physical body. Operating above the real-time nervous system and the dynamical body, the brain serves as the cognitive command center: it is the organ responsible for making sense of incoming sensory evidence and deciding what the physical body should attempt to do next.

To understand the engineering requirements of this cognitive layer, we must first contrast an embodied brain with a disembodied data center model. When a large language model in the cloud generates text, a hallucinated token carries no physical inertia; a user simply re-prompts the model, and the only cost incurred is digital compute. When an embodied machine operates in the physical world, its cognitive decisions govern moving mass that carries kinetic energy ($E_k = \frac{1}{2} m v^2$). In the physical domain, a cognitive error is not a software exception that can be caught in a `try-catch` block; it is a bent manipulator arm, a broken conveyor fixture, or a catastrophic collision with a human coworker.

To govern an embodied machine effectively in the open world, an embodied brain must satisfy five ideal properties:

First, it must possess open-world semantic generalizability. Rather than being confined to a narrow, pre-programmed lookup table of known objects, the brain must interpret open-vocabulary human language and generalize zero-shot across novel shapes, textures, and spatial arrangements.

Second, it must exhibit continuous sensory robustness. Real-world physical sensors operate under shifting sunlight, specular reflections, dynamic shadows, and camera lens dust. The cognitive architecture must smoothly absorb high-dimensional sensory noise without suffering discrete, brittle failures.

Third, it must maintain metric spatial-temporal grounding. Disembodied language models reason over abstract semantic concepts, but an embodied machine moves through three-dimensional Euclidean space. The brain must anchor its semantic concepts in metric coordinates, track objects through temporary visual occlusions, and model the continuous velocities of dynamic bodies. The metric pose of an object or robot link is described by the Special Euclidean Lie group $SE(3) = \mathbb{R}^3 \rtimes SO(3)$, parameterized by a translation vector $\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and an orthonormal rotation matrix $\mathbf{R} \in SO(3)$.

Fourth, it must achieve temporal multi-rate cadence decoupling. High-level reasoning and task planning are computationally demanding, requiring multi-billion-parameter models that deliberate at slow, human cadences ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$). Yet controlling physical mass requires continuous, reactive trajectory setpoints at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ to prevent dynamic drift. The cognitive architecture must cleanly bridge these disparate operational cadences without stalling the actuators.

Fifth, it must operate under bounded execution authority. Because statistical models are inherently uncalibrated under out-of-distribution shifts and prone to semantic hallucinations, the brain cannot hold direct authority over physical actuators. It must emit candidate proposals that remain strictly containable by downstream deterministic safety monitors.

The fundamental engineering question is: *what architectural paradigm can deliver these five ideal properties?*
<!-- END -->

## The Classical Wall {#sec-brain-3-2}

<!-- SECTION 3.2 -->
<!-- claim: Classical analytical methods provide formal guarantees in structured cages but shatter against the open world's combinatorial complexity. -->
<!-- covers: The classical tri-pillar: analytical dynamics (M*q_ddot + C*q_dot + g = tau), 3D CAD matching (ICP/RANSAC), and boolean state machine trees. -->
<!-- covers: Real-world image of structured industrial welding in automotive plant (#fig-industrial-welding). -->
<!-- covers: Strengths of classical control: formal Lyapunov stability, deterministic execution timing, and ISO 26262 certification in caged environments. -->
<!-- covers: The Classical Wall: combinatorial geometry explosion, single-pixel sensory brittleness, and the hand-authored rulebook bottleneck. -->
<!-- covers: Progressive disclosure and pure CMOS narrative without bullet lists. -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
For nearly a century, automated control and robotics approached cognition as an explicit geometric and analytical physics problem [@wiener1948cybernetics; @kalman1960new; @craig2005introduction]. Under this classical paradigm, engineers constructed mathematical representations from first principles.

Analytical kinematics and differential dynamics mapped desired end-effector motions into actuator torques using closed-form equations ($\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})\ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})\dot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q}) = \boldsymbol{\tau}$). Perception relied on matching hand-crafted 3D Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models against sensor point clouds using iterative closest point (ICP) or sample consensus (RANSAC) algorithms. High-level task logic was authored as explicit boolean state machines that dictated deterministic transitions between operational phases, such as approaching, aligning, grasping, and retracting.

![*Structured classical robotics regime (automotive body shop).* Multiple 6-DoF articulated industrial robots execute pre-programmed spot welding paths on stamped automotive chassis at the BMW Leipzig plant. Operating in a strictly calibrated environment with sub-millimeter repeatable fixtures and physical interlock safety cages, classical analytical controllers provide deterministic cycle timing and formal stability proofs. (Credit: BMW Group / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0 de).](figures/fig03_real_industrial_welding.jpg){#fig-industrial-welding fig-pos="t" width=85%}

Where the operational environment is strictly structured and bounded (@fig-industrial-welding), classical methods represent the pinnacle of dependable engineering. On an automated automotive assembly line, an industrial robot welds stamped steel panels where every workpiece arrives at an exact coordinate within sub-millimeter tolerances. Ambient lighting is tightly regulated by industrial fixtures, and human workers are excluded by physical interlock safety fences. In this controlled regime, classical algorithms provide complete mathematical transparency, microsecond execution timing, and provable stability certificates. An engineer can formally prove Lyapunov stability, guarantee that trajectories stay within joint torque bounds, and achieve structural code coverage under ISO 26262 without collecting a single demonstration.

Yet the moment an embodied machine leaves the structured factory cage to operate in homes, warehouses, construction sites, or agricultural fields, this classical paradigm hits what roboticists describe as the Classical Wall [@brooks1991intelligence; @levine2018learning]. The physical world is not a sterile CAD drawing; it is continuous, deformable, uncataloged, and endlessly variable.

The first breakdown occurs in the combinatorial explosion of geometry. In a commercial logistics warehouse handling hundreds of thousands of retail goods, authoring CAD models, mesh templates, and grasp points for every bottle, wrapped package, and flexible garment is impossible. Discretizing orientations, frictional properties, and contact permutations across overlapping, deformable items creates a combinatorial space exceeding billions of distinct geometric configurations that cannot be captured in hand-crafted templates.

The second breakdown arises from sensory brittleness. Classical computer vision relies on hand-crafted feature extractors, such as edge filters, Harris corners, or surface normal thresholds. When ambient sunlight shifts, water puddles create specular reflections, or an object is partially obscured by dust, discrete feature detectors fracture. A single missing edge causes a planar segmentation algorithm to bridge across two distinct physical objects, commanding a gripper to pinch an empty void.

![*Unstructured open-world robotics regime (urban search and rescue).* A mobile rescue robot navigates an obstacle course with irregular inclines, loose wooden debris, and unpredictable visual occlusions. In such open-ended environments, pre-authored 3D CAD models and deterministic state machines shatter, requiring physical AI systems to infer spatial affordances and terrain traversability directly from multimodal sensory streams. (Credit: TU Darmstadt Rescue Robotics / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0).](figures/fig03_real_unstructured_rescue.jpg){#fig-unstructured-rescue fig-pos="t" width=85%}

The third breakdown is the engineering bottleneck of hand-authored logic. In classical systems, the machine's operational capability is bounded by the human engineer's ability to anticipate every physical edge case in advance. When an unexpected variation occurs—such as a bent bracket, a scuffed label, or an unfamiliar obstacle—the hand-authored rulebook contains no matching branch, causing the machine to halt, drop its payload, or fail catastrophically.
<!-- END -->

## Learned Representations {#sec-brain-3-3}

<!-- SECTION 3.3 -->
<!-- claim: The robotics and ML community embraced learned representations because they solve four foundational challenges: generalizability, sensory robustness, complex contact dynamics, and empirical scaling. -->
<!-- covers: Pillar 1: Open-World Semantic Generalizability (VLMs/VLAs, zero-shot language grounding). -->
<!-- covers: Pillar 2: Continuous Sensory Robustness (continuous latent manifolds absorbing visual noise). -->
<!-- covers: Pillar 3: Complex Multi-Contact & Deformable Dynamics (cloth, cables, fluids, friction). -->
<!-- covers: Pillar 4: Empirical Scaling & The Bitter Lesson (compute & demonstration data replacing hand-engineering). -->
<!-- covers: Grounding in a canonical dual-arm testbed (#fig-aloha-manipulator). -->
<!-- covers: Progressive disclosure: building clear intuition before deep pipeline mechanics. -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
Physical AI arose to dismantle the classical wall by replacing rigid human-authored heuristics with deep neural representations fitted directly to multimodal sensory data. In the embodied AI and robotics community, this transition was driven by four foundational pillars:

The first pillar is open-world semantic generalizability. Classical controllers are inherently narrow: an inverse kinematics solver can move an end-effector to coordinate $(x, y, z)$, but it possesses zero semantic understanding of what resides at that location or how surrounding objects relate to human tasks. Modern vision-language-action foundation models project open-vocabulary natural language instructions and high-resolution camera streams into shared semantic embeddings [@driess2023palme; @brohan2023rt1; @brohan2023rt2; @kim2024openvla]. When commanded to "wipe the coffee spill from the counter and stow the mug in the drying rack," a learned model parses the unstructured scene into functional affordances, identifying the graspable handle of an unfamiliar mug and the planar boundaries of the liquid stain without requiring an engineer to provide a 3D CAD model or write a single line of procedural code.

The second pillar is continuous sensory robustness. While classical algorithms suffer from boolean brittleness—where a minor shift in lighting or surface texture flips a discrete classification branch—deep neural networks project high-dimensional sensory inputs onto smooth, continuous latent manifolds. Variations in ambient illumination, background clutter, shadow transitions, and camera perspective produce bounded displacements in latent space rather than catastrophic categorical jumps.

The third pillar is the ability to handle complex multi-contact and deformable dynamics. Many physical manipulation tasks—such as folding laundry, routing flexible wire harnesses through car doors, or scooping granular media—involve non-smooth contact mechanics, variable friction, and infinite-dimensional deformations that cannot be modeled in closed-form differential equations. By learning directly from physical teleoperation demonstrations, neural policies acquire intuitive physical behaviors that naturally exploit compliance and surface contacts.

![*Authentic bimanual robotic policy testbed.* A canonical dual-arm bimanual teleoperation workcell featuring two 6-DoF follower arms, two leader arms for kinesthetic teleoperation, multi-view RGB cameras (overhead and wrist-mounted RealSense modules), and mechanical parallel grippers mounted to an extruded aluminum structural frame. The setup demonstrates how physical AI policies ingest synchronized high-dimensional multi-camera streams to generate continuous end-effector trajectories, requiring deterministic safety governors and reachability filters to prevent self-collisions and motor over-torquing during closed-loop execution. (Credit: Stanford University & Google DeepMind, CC-BY / Apache 2.0).](figures/fig03_real_aloha_manipulator.png){#fig-aloha-manipulator fig-pos="t" width=85%}

The fourth pillar is empirical scaling with data and compute. As articulated by Richard Sutton in *The Bitter Lesson* [@sutton2019bitter], methods that leverage general computation and large-scale learning consistently surpass hand-engineered domain heuristics over time. By training high-capacity transformer architectures across millions of diverse robotic teleoperation demonstrations (@fig-aloha-manipulator) and web-scale multimodal datasets [@zhao2023learning; @chi2023diffusionpolicy], physical AI systems steadily improve in dexterity and resilience without requiring engineers to manually re-author control logic for each new task.

![*Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architecture and unprivileged proposal pipeline.* (1) Multimodal ingestion tokenizes multi-view camera streams ($224 \times 224 \times 3$ RGB), natural language task instructions, and proprioceptive joint states ($\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}}$). (2) A high-capacity transformer backbone ($7\text{B--}55\text{B}$ parameters) fuses spatial and semantic tokens across self-attention layers, operating on embedded edge silicon (such as a canonical heterogeneous application MPU with dedicated tensor coprocessors). (3) The policy emits unprivileged candidate action proposals via discrete token binning (single-step waypoints) or diffusion action chunking (continuous $H$-step trajectory splines). (4) Downstream real-time safety monitors on isolated microcontrollers evaluate physical invariants at $1000\text{ Hz}$ before granting actuator execution permission.](figures/fig03_vla_architecture.svg){#fig-vla-architecture fig-pos="t" width=95%}

As structured in the modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) paradigm (@fig-vla-architecture), an embodied foundation model is not an opaque monolith, but a structured four-stage neural pipeline that transforms sensory fluxes into motor candidates:

1. **Spatial & Semantic Tokenization (Information from the Left):** Raw camera frames ($224 \times 224 \times 3$) enter a spatial vision backbone (such as DINOv2 or SigLIP), which partitions the image into a $14 \times 14$ grid of $16 \times 16$ pixel patches. Each patch is flattened and linearly projected into a $D$-dimensional visual embedding $\mathbf{z}_{\text{vision}}$. Concurrently, natural language task instructions are parsed into subword tokens $[\mathbf{t}_1, \dots, \mathbf{t}_L]$, while continuous proprioceptive joint encoders ($\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}}$) are projected into matching state tokens $\mathbf{z}_{\text{state}}$.
2. **Multimodal Alignment & Fusion (The Backbone):** The visual, linguistic, and physical state tokens are concatenated into a unified sequence $[\mathbf{z}_{\text{vision}} \,|\, \mathbf{z}_{\text{text}} \,|\, \mathbf{z}_{\text{state}}]$ and processed through 32–80 transformer self-attention layers. Cross-attention mechanisms bind linguistic intent ("grasp the screwdriver") directly to the spatial coordinates of visual patches.
3. **Action Decoding (Information to the Right):** Instead of generating autoregressive text words, the final hidden activation $\mathbf{h}_t$ feeds an **Unprivileged Action Decoder Head**. This head projects the latent state into continuous motor action candidates—either single-step delta poses or multi-step continuous trajectory chunks $\hat{\mathbf{a}}_{t:t+H} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_a}$ (comprising 3D position deltas $\Delta \mathbf{p}$, rotation increments $\Delta \boldsymbol{\theta}$, and gripper actuation flags).
4. **The Privilege Boundary (Isolation from Motors):** Crucially, the model's output is an unverified candidate proposal ($p_t$). It carries zero direct hardware permission to energize motor coils until downstream real-time enforcers on isolated silicon verify kinematic and kinetic invariants at $1000\text{ Hz}$.[^fn-trans-unprivileged-control]
<!-- END -->

## The Cognitive Pipeline {#sec-brain-3-4}

<!-- SECTION 3.4 -->
<!-- claim: The learned cognitive pipeline transforms raw physical fluxes into candidate trajectory proposals across five sequential stages. -->
<!-- covers: Horizontal Left-to-Right Pipeline Diagram (#fig-cognitive-pipeline). -->
<!-- covers: Five Stages: Ingestion, Perception, Memory, Intent, Planning. -->
<!-- covers: Concrete example prompt in Intent (decomposing mission into subgoals and leases). -->
<!-- covers: Action chunking progressive disclosure (why single-step inference stutters mass vs multi-step chunks). -->
<!-- covers: Seamless narrative weaving archetype groundings and systems engineering implications. -->
<!-- covers: Vector Figure: Five Handoffs (#fig-five-handoffs). -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
To architect a learned cognitive pipeline, we must trace how information flows from raw physical sensations to actionable trajectory setpoints. Rather than treating the brain as an unstructured end-to-end black box, a dependable physical AI architecture organizes cognition into five sequential stages (@fig-cognitive-pipeline and @fig-five-handoffs): Ingestion, Perception, Memory, Intent, and Planning.

![*The cognitive flow of physical AI: End-to-end left-to-right pipeline.* Information flows sequentially from physical sensors through Ingestion (tokenization), Perception (spatial geometry & affordances), Memory (persistent world model belief), Intent (deliberative goal leases), and Planning (multi-step action chunking), crossing the Proposal–Permission boundary to downstream real-time reflexes.](figures/fig03_cognitive_pipeline_horizontal.svg){#fig-cognitive-pipeline fig-pos="t" width=95%}

### Ingestion and Representation {.unnumbered}

Cognition begins at the physical boundary where environmental energy is transduced into digital bitstreams. Photons strike active-pixel CMOS sensors across 2D camera grids, infrared pulses measure photon time-of-flight in depth cameras, and micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) in inertial measurement units (IMUs) sample accelerations and angular velocities.

The ingestion stage translates these heterogeneous, high-bandwidth bitstreams into normalized numerical embeddings. Modern embodied foundation models utilize Vision Transformers (ViTs) to process spatial visual inputs [@dosovitskiy2020image]. A raw image frame $\mathbf{I} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$ is partitioned into a sequence of non-overlapping 2D patches $\mathbf{x}_p \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times (P^2 \cdot C)}$, where $P \times P$ is the patch resolution (typically $14 \times 14$ or $16 \times 16$ pixels) and $N = (HW)/P^2$ is the resulting token sequence length. Each flattened patch is linearly projected into a continuous latent space of dimension $D$, concatenated with learned positional embeddings to preserve spatial geometry, and interleaved with tokenized natural language instructions. Continuous proprioceptive state vectors (such as joint positions $\mathbf{q}$, velocities $\dot{\mathbf{q}}$, and gripper opening widths) are similarly normalized and projected into matching token spaces, producing a unified multimodal token sequence that serves as the common input for downstream reasoning.[^fn-arch-curriculum-deepdives]

Consider how this operates across the three machine archetypes:

- *Mobile systems:* A quadruped traversing rubble synchronizes four RGB-D cameras streaming at $30\text{ fps}$ ($>740\text{ MB/s}$ raw data) alongside 12 joint encoders sampled at $1000\text{ Hz}$. Ingestion tokenizes each visual frame into hundreds of patch embeddings while downsampling and embedding the high-frequency joint state stream into a unified temporal sequence.
- *Manipulators:* A dual-arm workstation ingests synchronized stereo wrist camera feeds ($60\text{ fps}$) and 14-DoF joint positions, tokenizing visual patches and motor states into aligned input tokens for end-effector coordination.
- *Process / energy systems:* A continuous chemical reactor ingests thousands of analog thermocouple, pressure transducer, and mass flow meter channels at $100\text{ Hz}$, normalizing heterogeneous sensor calibrations into a rolling multivariate state tensor.

This ingestion pipeline places substantial demands on data bandwidth and memory throughput. Streaming multiple high-definition camera feeds generates gigabytes of raw pixel data every second. Systems engineers must implement efficient frame buffering, sensor exposure synchronization, and spatial patch pooling to keep data moving smoothly before cognitive reasoning begins.

### Perception and Spatial Grounding {.unnumbered}

The perception stage extracts metric structure, semantic identity, and spatial affordances from the ingested tokens. Rather than treating sensory data as an unstructured bag of visual features, perception grounds representations in the 3D Euclidean space ($SE(3)$) of the physical workspace.

Using dense self-supervised representations such as DINOv2 [@oquab2023dinov2] alongside learned spatial decoders, the perception layer isolates distinct physical entities, segments object boundaries, estimates metric 3D bounding boxes, and reconstructs surface normal vectors. Crucially, perception extracts spatial affordances: functional geometric fields that describe where and how an object can be physically engaged. For a drill, perception identifies not merely a generic class label, but the 3D position and orientation of the handle grasp axis, the trigger contact surface, and the drill bit tip. This transforms ungrounded pixel arrays into actionable spatial entities referenced to the robot's base coordinate frame.

When a mobile manipulator is commanded to retrieve a torque wrench from a cluttered workbench, perception isolates the tool from surrounding background clutter, predicts its 6-DoF pose ($SE(3)$ transformation matrix $\mathbf{T}_{\text{base}}^{\text{tool}}$), and outputs a continuous heatmap over the handle indicating valid gripper pinch contacts.

In practice, perception is highly vulnerable to sensor calibration drift. If camera mounting screws loosen by half a millimeter or structural arm links deflect under payload weight, the transformation matrix between the camera optical center and the robot base frame drifts. This introduces metric scale errors that cause precision grippers to miss targets or strike work surfaces. Systems engineers must implement online hand-eye recalibration routines and maintain spatial uncertainty covariances alongside raw point estimates.

### Memory and Spatial-Temporal Belief {.unnumbered}

A physical agent cannot act reliably from a single instantaneous snapshot of the world. Objects pass behind visual occlusions, cameras pan away from manipulated targets, and physical bodies possess dynamic momentum that cannot be inferred from a single frame.

The memory stage maintains a persistent, rolling spatial-temporal belief of the environment. It tracks object identities across time, correlates visual features with geometric coordinate frames, and updates 3D volumetric representations such as Truncated Signed Distance Fields (TSDFs), Language Embedded Radiance Fields (LERF) [@kerr2023lerf], or 3D Gaussian Splatting maps. By fusing historical observations across a sliding temporal window, memory maintains accurate state estimates even during complete visual occlusion, computes linear and angular object velocities, and tracks operational context across multi-step tasks.

For a quadruped traversing a rocky ledge, the forward-facing camera points toward the horizon, losing sight of the immediate ground beneath its front feet. The memory stage preserves the reconstructed 3D surface geometry of the terrain, enabling the robot to securely place its hind feet onto footholds it observed several seconds earlier.

Maintaining dense volumetric belief states introduces significant memory footprints. Storing high-resolution 3D voxel grids or radiance field parameters requires substantial storage capacity, competing directly with the memory needed to run large neural network models. Furthermore, belief representations degrade in freshness over time: if a dynamic obstacle moves while occluded, an un-decayed memory belief causes the robot to plan around a "phantom" obstacle or collide with an unobserved intruder. Systems engineers must enforce explicit temporal decay rates on spatial belief states to reflect physical entropy.

### Intent and Deliberative Reasoning {.unnumbered}

Given a persistent belief of the world and a high-level mission prompt, the intent stage performs semantic reasoning and task decomposition. Because open-vocabulary foundation models operate over vast parameter spaces (typically 7B to 70B parameters), deliberative reasoning occurs at slow, human-scale cadences ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$).

To understand how intent operates, imagine a human operator issues a natural language mission prompt:

$$\text{"Clear the table by placing the ceramic mug in the sink and throwing the paper napkin into the trash bin."}$$

The intent layer cannot execute this directive in a single leap. Using embodied reasoning architectures such as SayCan [@ahn2022saycan], VoxPoser [@huang2023voxposer], or Code as Policies [@liang2023code], the deliberative model queries the active world memory and decomposes the mission into an ordered sequence of discrete subgoals: first approach the mug, grasp the handle, transport it to the sink coordinate frame, and release contact, before turning toward the napkin.

Rather than commanding actuator voltages directly, the intent stage packages each subgoal into a formal, cryptographically bounded **Intent Lease** ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$). An intent lease specifies the active target entity, defines a bounded spatial corridor outside which motion is unauthorized, and establishes an explicit expiration timestamp ($t_{\text{expire}}$).

| Field Name             | Type            | Unit                   | Description & Structural Invariants                                                                              |
|:-----------------------|:----------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `lease_id`             | `uint64_t`      | —                      | Monotonically increasing 64-bit sequence identifier                                                              |
| `target_entity_id`     | `uint32_t`      | —                      | Hash of target entity in persistent spatial memory                                                               |
| `pose_target_se3`      | `float32[4][4]` | $\text{m}, \text{rad}$ | Valid $\text{SE}(3)$ pose matrix: $\mathbf{R} \in \text{SO}(3), \det(\mathbf{R})=1, \mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ |
| `spatial_corridor_box` | `float32[6]`    | $\text{m}$             | Authorized 3D bounding box $[\mathbf{p}_{\min}, \mathbf{p}_{\max}] \in \mathbb{R}^6$                             |
| `t_generated_ns`       | `uint64_t`      | $\text{ns}$            | PTP monotonic hardware timestamp at deliberation completion                                                      |
| `t_expire_ns`          | `uint64_t`      | $\text{ns}$            | Hard expiration timestamp; enforces $t_{\text{expire}} - t_{\text{gen}} \le \tau_{\text{valid}}$                 |
| `max_permissible_jerk` | `float32`       | $\text{m/s}^3$         | Maximum allowable end-effector / joint jerk magnitude                                                            |
| `hmac_signature`       | `uint8_t[32]`   | bytes                  | SHA-256 deliberation cryptographic contract signature                                                            |
: Intent Lease Contract Schema ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$). {#tbl-03-intent-lease-schema}

This deliberative cadence creates an inherent freshness gap. If a large vision-language foundation model requires $400\text{ ms}$ to generate an intent lease, the physical world has moved during that inference window. If the target mug was bumped or a coworker walked between the robot and the sink, the intent lease is partially stale before it reaches the motion planner. Systems engineers must bound intent lease lifetimes ($\tau_{\text{valid}}$) and enforce strict timeout rejection gates at execution time.

### Planning and Action Chunking {.unnumbered}

An intent lease specifies what operational goal to pursue, but it provides no continuous motor trajectories and no guarantee that intervening motion satisfies physical kinematic limits. The planning stage converts the active intent lease into candidate joint trajectories or end-effector motion setpoints via an **Unprivileged Action Decoder Head**.

To understand how planning is executed on physical silicon, we must treat deep neural policies not as abstract mathematical functions, but as physical compute workloads running on embedded accelerators—such as a canonical high-performance heterogeneous edge System-on-Chip (SoC) with integrated GPU tensor cores and dedicated deep learning accelerators—bounded by memory bus bandwidth, silicon thermals, and electrical power.

Consider what happens if a robot attempts to generate continuous motor actions one discrete step at a time through an autoregressive foundation model (such as a 7-billion parameter Vision-Language-Action network). In autoregressive decoding, generating each individual action token requires the processor to stream every parameter of the network from external Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM) across silicon bus traces into on-chip cache and vector registers.

For a 7B parameter model stored in 16-bit floating-point precision (FP16), the weight matrix occupies:

$$M_{\text{weights}} = 7 \times 10^9 \text{ parameters} \times 2\text{ bytes/parameter} = 14.0\text{ GB}$$

On an embedded edge compute module equipped with a 256-bit wide LPDDR5 memory interface delivering a theoretical peak bandwidth of $B_{\text{mem}} = 204.8\text{ GB/s}$, the minimum physical time required simply to sweep those weights across the bus once is:[^fn-hw-lpddr5-bandwidth]

$$t_{\text{stream}} = \frac{M_{\text{weights}}}{B_{\text{mem}}} = \frac{14.0\text{ GB}}{204.8\text{ GB/s}} \approx 68.4\text{ ms}$$

This physical reality imposes an unyielding frequency ceiling: even if arithmetic computation consumed zero nanoseconds, the memory bus alone caps single-step token generation at an absolute maximum of $f_{\text{max}} = 1 / 0.0684\text{ s} \approx 14.6\text{ Hz}$. When we account for sensory attention ingestion, KV-cache lookup, and operating system scheduling, live single-token inference drops to $1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$. If an embodied manipulator attempted to control moving mass at $5\text{ Hz}$, the actuators would freeze and stutter between consecutive ticks like a buffering video stream, causing dynamic drift, severe contact instability, and dropped payloads.

We can analyze this bottleneck formally through the **Roofline Model** [@williams2009roofline],[^fn-trans-roofline-ai] which bounds attainable compute performance $P$ (in FLOP/s) by the processor's peak arithmetic throughput $P_{\text{peak}}$ and its memory bandwidth $B_{\text{mem}}$:

$$P = \min\left(P_{\text{peak}}, \; I \cdot B_{\text{mem}}\right)$$

where $I$ is the operational arithmetic intensity defined as:

$$I = \frac{\text{Floating-Point Operations (FLOPs)}}{\text{Memory Data Transferred (Bytes)}}$$

In single-step autoregressive generation, reading a 2-byte weight to perform a single multiply-accumulate operation (2 FLOPs) yields an arithmetic intensity of:

$$I_{\text{single}} \approx \frac{2\text{ FLOPs}}{2\text{ bytes}} = 1.0\text{ FLOP/byte}$$

Because this intensity is orders of magnitude below the accelerator's saturation knee ($I_{\text{knee}} = P_{\text{peak}} / B_{\text{mem}} \approx 1340\text{ FLOP/byte}$ for a canonical $275\text{ TFLOP/s}$ heterogeneous SoC), single-step inference is trapped deep in the **memory-bandwidth-bound regime**.[^fn-math-roofline-derivation] The tensor accelerator achieves less than $0.1\%$ of its peak compute throughput, spending over $99\%$ of its time stalled waiting for DRAM memory transfers.

::: {.callout-definition title="The Memory Wall Ceiling"}
The **Memory Wall Ceiling** is the absolute upper bound on model evaluation frequency ($f_{\max} = B_{\text{mem}} / M_{\text{weights}}$) imposed by external DRAM bus bandwidth when streaming non-resident neural network weights into on-chip vector registers. In single-step autoregressive inference, operational arithmetic intensity collapses to $I \approx 1.0\text{ FLOP/byte}$, stranding execution units in memory-stalled idle states and forcing the control rate below the mechanical resonance of the physical body.
:::

![*The Patterson roofline model and embodied memory wall.* Operational arithmetic intensity ($I = \text{FLOPs}/\text{Byte}$) plotted against attainable execution throughput on embedded edge silicon (a canonical heterogeneous SoC, $204.8\text{ GB/s}$ LPDDR5 DRAM bandwidth, $275\text{ TFLOP/s}$ compute ceiling). Single-step autoregressive foundation model inference operates at $I \approx 1.0\text{ FLOP/Byte}$, trapped deep in the memory-bound regime where execution units stall $>99\%$ of the time waiting for DRAM weight sweeps ($t_{\text{stream}} = 68.4\text{ ms} \implies f_{\max} \le 14.6\text{ Hz}$). Action chunking ($H = 32\text{--}64$) increases operational arithmetic intensity $50\times$ to $I \approx 50\text{--}150\text{ FLOP/Byte}$, amortizing parameter transfers across time to bridge slow deliberative foundation models with fast $1000\text{ Hz}$ real-time reflexes. INT8/FP8 quantization further doubles arithmetic intensity while halving DRAM bus power dissipation.](figures/fig03_patterson_roofline.svg){#fig-patterson-roofline fig-pos="t" width=95%}

To break through this memory wall and deliver smooth, high-frequency continuous control, modern physical AI policies employ **Action Chunking** [@zhao2023learning; @chi2023diffusionpolicy]:[^fn-trans-vla-concept] predicting a sequence of $H$ future continuous actions $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H} = [\mathbf{a}_t, \mathbf{a}_{t+1}, \dots, \mathbf{a}_{t+H}]$ in a single neural forward pass or fixed diffusion denoising schedule, amortizing parameter memory transfers across multiple real-time execution cycles.

Instead of fetching billions of weights from DRAM to predict a single scalar action for the immediate millisecond, the planning policy (such as Action Chunking with Transformers [ACT], Diffusion Policy, or Flow Matching) generates an entire temporal horizon of continuous actions $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H} = [\mathbf{a}_t, \mathbf{a}_{t+1}, \dots, \mathbf{a}_{t+H}] \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_a}$ (typically $H = 16\text{--}64$ steps spanning $320\text{--}1280\text{ ms}$) in a single forward pass or fixed denoising schedule ($K = 10\text{--}16$ diffusion steps).[^fn-math-action-chunking]

| Field Name            | Type            | Unit                           | Description & Structural Invariants                                     |             |                        |
|:----------------------|:----------------|:-------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| `chunk_id`            | `uint64_t`      | —                              | Monotonically increasing trajectory sequence ID                         |             |                        |
| `parent_lease_id`     | `uint64_t`      | —                              | Must match active unexpired Intent Lease ID                             |             |                        |
| `horizon_steps` ($H$) | `uint32_t`      | count                          | Temporal horizon length of candidate waypoints (e.g., $32$)             |             |                        |
| `step_duration_dt`    | `float32`       | $\text{s}$                     | Fixed inter-waypoint control sampling period $\Delta t = 0.02\text{ s}$ |             |                        |
| `trajectory_q`        | `float32[H][N]` | $\text{rad}$ or $\text{m}$     | Planned joint positions for all $N$ degrees of freedom                  |             |                        |
| `trajectory_qdot`     | `float32[H][N]` | $\text{rad/s}$ or $\text{m/s}$ | Planned velocities satisfying $\                                        | \dot{q}_j\  | \le \dot{q}_{\max,j}$  |
| `trajectory_qddot`    | `float32[H][N]` | $\text{rad/s}^2$               | Planned accelerations satisfying $\                                     | \ddot{q}_j\ | \le \ddot{q}_{\max,j}$ |
| `t_generation_ns`     | `uint64_t`      | $\text{ns}$                    | PTP synchronized exposure timestamp of source observation               |             |                        |
: Action Chunk Trajectory Packet Schema ($\mathbf{A}_{\text{chunk}}$). {#tbl-03-action-chunk-schema}

As structured in the trajectory packet schema (@tbl-03-action-chunk-schema), by processing the entire trajectory horizon simultaneously across parallel matrix multiplications, action chunking increases the operational arithmetic intensity by orders of magnitude ($I \ge 50\text{--}100\text{ FLOP/byte}$). This shifts execution out of the memory-bound bottleneck and into the **compute-bound roofline plateau**, saturating tensor cores and allowing generative policies to synthesize candidate trajectory chunks at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ on compact embedded power envelopes ($15\text{--}60\text{ W}$).

For example, when a canonical bimanual manipulator threads a flexible USB cable (@fig-aloha-manipulator), it executes a 32-step action chunk. The policy emits coordinated 14-DoF joint setpoints that smoothly align both grippers, flex the cable, and insert the connector without pausing between individual control cycles.

However, action chunking introduces the critical systems challenge of **chunk seam continuity**. Because each action chunk is generated independently from rolling sensory observations, the tail of chunk $k$ and the head of chunk $k+1$ may exhibit slight positional and velocity discrepancies. If a controller concatenated these chunks directly, the resulting step-discontinuities in acceleration would inject massive jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}}$) into the physical linkages, causing acoustic vibration, cycloidal pin wear, and motor overcurrent faults.

To guarantee smooth physical execution, systems implement **Temporal Ensembling** (exponentially weighted averaging across overlapping chunk predictions):

$$\mathbf{a}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{\min(t, H-1)} w_i \, \mathbf{a}_{t \mid t-i}}{\sum_{i=0}^{\min(t, H-1)} w_i}, \quad w_i = \exp(-m \cdot i)$$

where $\mathbf{a}_{t \mid t-i}$ represents the action predicted for time step $t$ by the action chunk initiated at time $t-i$, and $m > 0$ is a tunable temporal discount factor. The resulting smoothed waypoints are interpolated via quintic ($C^2$) splines by the downstream real-time nervous system at $1000\text{ Hz}$, ensuring continuous positions, velocities, and accelerations across all actuator joints while preserving valid $SE(3)$ transformations (using Lie algebra $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ exponential mapping or Spherical Linear Interpolation to keep rotation matrices strictly orthonormal).

The complete operational loop spanning intent reasoning, action chunk synthesis, and deterministic safety arbitration is formalized in Algorithm 3.1.

::: {.callout-algorithm  title="Algorithm 3.1: Two-Speed Brain Deliberation and Safety Enforcement"}
**Inputs:** Multi-view visual frames $\mathbf{I}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$, proprioceptive state $(\mathbf{q}_t, \dot{\mathbf{q}}_t)$, mission prompt $M$, spatial corridor $\text{Box}_{\text{safe}}$, stopping distance model $d_{\text{stop}}(v)$.

**Outputs:** Real-time motor command $\mathbf{u}_t$ written to hardware PWM registers.

**Structural Invariants:**

1. *Authority Invariant:* No learned proposal $\mathbf{p}_t$ directly modifies actuator registers without passing deterministic safety validation.
2. *Temporal Freshness Invariant:* If $(t_{\text{now}} - t_{\text{transduction}} > \Delta t_{\text{fresh}})$, candidate proposal is rejected and deterministic holding reflex is engaged.
3. *Dynamic Clearance Invariant:* Motor torque is energized if and only if $d_{\text{stop}}(v) \le D_{\text{clear}}$.

**Execution Pipeline:**

1. **System 2: Intent Deliberation ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$ on unprivileged Host MPU):**
   * If ($\text{active\_lease} == \text{NULL}$ or $t_{\text{now}} \ge \text{active\_lease}.t_{\text{expire}}$):
     * Tokenize visual observation $\mathbf{I}_t$ and query 3D world memory (TSDF / 3DGS).
     * Evaluate Vision-Language-Action backbone to decompose task prompt $M$ into next subgoal.
     * Construct Intent Lease $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$ with spatial corridor $\text{Box}_{\text{safe}}$ and expiration $t_{\text{expire}} = t_{\text{now}} + \tau_{\text{valid}}$.
     * Cryptographically sign $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$ and dispatch to System 1.5 trajectory planner.
2. **System 1.5: Action Chunk Trajectory Synthesis ($20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ on Neural Accelerator):**
   * Ingest joint states $(\mathbf{q}_t, \dot{\mathbf{q}}_t)$ and active unexpired $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$.
   * Evaluate Diffusion Policy / ACT backbone to synthesize $H$-step chunk $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$.
   * Apply temporal ensembling across overlapping chunk horizons:
     $$\mathbf{a}_t = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{\min(t, H-1)} w_i \, \mathbf{a}_{t \mid t-i}}{\sum w_i}, \quad w_i = \exp(-m \cdot i)$$

   * Fit $\mathcal{C}^2$ quintic splines through waypoints and package into $\mathbf{A}_{\text{chunk}}$.
3. **System 1: Hard Real-Time Deterministic Reflex Gate ($1000\text{ Hz}$ on Bare-Metal MCU):**
   * On every $1\text{ ms}$ timer interrupt:
     * Sample calibrated joint encoders and hardware distance sensors.
     * Fetch candidate setpoint $\mathbf{a}_t$ from active $\mathbf{A}_{\text{chunk}}$.
     * *Evaluate Rejection Gates:*
       * If $(t_{\text{now}} > \mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}.t_{\text{expire}}) \implies \text{REJECT}(\text{LEASE\_EXPIRED})$
       * If $(\mathbf{a}_t \notin \text{Box}_{\text{safe}} \lor |\dot{\mathbf{q}}| > \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}) \implies \text{REJECT}(\text{KINEMATIC\_LIMIT})$
       * If $(d_{\text{stop}}(v) > D_{\text{clear}}) \implies \text{REJECT}(\text{COLLISION\_IMMINENT})$
     * *Arbitration Verdict:*
       * If all checks pass: Permission **GRANTED** $\implies \mathbf{u}_t = \mathbf{a}_t \to \text{PWM Registers}$.
       * Else: Permission **DENIED** $\implies \mathbf{u}_t = \text{SafeStopReflex}() \to \text{Controlled Braking}$.
:::

::: {.callout-math title="The LPDDR5 Memory Wall and Action Chunking Speedup"}
How does Action Chunking overcome the memory bus bottleneck on an embedded physical AI compute module?

*1. The single-token memory bottleneck.*
Consider a 7-billion parameter Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policy stored in 16-bit precision (FP16) on an embedded edge System-on-Chip (e.g., a canonical heterogeneous SoC with a 256-bit LPDDR5 interface):

- Weight footprint: $M_{\text{weights}} = 7 \times 10^9 \text{ params} \times 2\text{ bytes} = 14.0\text{ GB}$.
- Theoretical memory bandwidth: $B_{\text{peak}} = 204.8\text{ GB/s}$.
- Realistic sustained DRAM bandwidth (accounting for $\sim 70\%$ bus scheduling efficiency and row-turnaround delays): $B_{\text{sustained}} \approx 143.4\text{ GB/s}$.

Minimum streaming latency to fetch the weights from DRAM across the silicon bus once:
$$t_{\text{stream}} = \frac{14.0\text{ GB}}{143.4\text{ GB/s}} \approx 97.6\text{ ms}$$

Maximum attainable control frequency for single-step autoregressive token generation:
$$f_{\text{single}} = \frac{1}{t_{\text{stream}}} \approx \frac{1}{0.0976\text{ s}} \approx 10.2\text{ Hz}$$
When accounting for ViT image tokenization ($15\text{ ms}$) and KV-cache lookups, live single-step frequency drops to $1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$. This is far too slow to stabilize a robotic limb or mobile chassis without severe mechanical stuttering.

*2. The action chunking amortization.*
Instead of predicting one action step per DRAM weight sweep, the policy generates an action chunk of $H = 32$ future time steps ($\Delta t = 20\text{ ms}$, spanning a $640\text{ ms}$ trajectory horizon) in a single neural forward pass.

- Number of weight memory sweeps: 1 sweep ($97.6\text{ ms}$).
- Parallel matrix multiplications across $H$ steps reuse weights resident in on-chip SRAM/caches, elevating arithmetic intensity from $I \approx 1.0\text{ FLOP/byte}$ to $I \ge 65\text{ FLOP/byte}$.
- Amortized compute latency per control step:
$$\tau_{\text{step}} = \frac{t_{\text{stream}}}{H} = \frac{97.6\text{ ms}}{32\text{ steps}} \approx 3.05\text{ ms/step}$$

*3. Physical AI systems impact.*
By amortizing weight streaming across the temporal chunk horizon, the effective control generation rate climbs from $10.2\text{ Hz}$ to:
$$f_{\text{effective}} = \frac{1}{\tau_{\text{step}}} \approx 328\text{ Hz (amortized)}$$
The embedded compute module synthesizes a new 32-step chunk every $100\text{ ms}$ ($10\text{ Hz}$ background cadence), providing a continuous stream of overlapping waypoints to the $1000\text{ Hz}$ spline interpolator with over $80\%$ spare processor duty cycle for real-time safety monitoring.
:::

::: {.callout-rule title="Embodied Cognition Guidelines"}
1. **The Autoregressive Actuator Stall:** Never drive physical motor loops directly from single-token autoregressive generation; DRAM streaming latency ($t_{\text{stream}} = M_{\text{weights}}/B_{\text{mem}}$) will starve the actuators below the body's resonant frequency.
2. **The Arithmetic Intensity Threshold:** If your policy forward pass achieves an arithmetic intensity below $50\text{ FLOP/byte}$ on embedded silicon, you are paying for high-performance tensor cores that spend over $90\%$ of their clock cycles idle in DRAM read queues.
3. **The Proposal–Permission Boundary:** The learned brain proposes candidate intent and trajectories in unconstrained software coordinates; the deterministic reflex engine grants physical execution permission in verified SI units.
4. **Softmax Is Not Physical Probability:** Exponentiated logits sum to one by mathematical definition, not physical truth; never gate safety-critical actuators on raw neural confidence without empirical calibration (ECE) and deterministic geometric fallback monitors.
:::

![The canonical five handoffs architecture and boundary rejection gates vs. collapsed end-to-end latent pipeline. (Panel A) The canonical modular chain enforces five distinct functional contracts: Observe (timestamped raw evidence), Estimate (metric state belief and covariance), Intend (semantic goal lease with expiration), Plan (candidate action chunk with $C^2$ spline bounds), and Enforce (active-set barrier QP solver). Each interface features a dedicated rejection gate (RG-1 through RG-5) that intercepts dropped packets, tracking divergence, expired leases, kinematic infeasibilities, or barrier violations before unprivileged proposals (dashed paths) can reach physical actuators. (Panel B) A collapsed end-to-end policy maps raw pixels directly to uninspected motor torques, forfeiting four critical intermediate inspection points and transferring the entire burden of sensory validation, state estimation, and lease verification onto low-level reflex filters.](figures/fig03_five_handoffs.svg){#fig-five-handoffs fig-pos="t" width=90%}
<!-- END -->

## Cognitive Vulnerabilities {#sec-brain-3-5}

<!-- SECTION 3.5 -->
<!-- claim: Learned brains fail through distinct, predictable cognitive vulnerabilities that require a strict Proposal-Permission architectural boundary. -->
<!-- covers: The loss of formal mathematical verifiability and the community schism. -->
<!-- covers: Four core cognitive failure modes: Semantic Hallucinations, Softmax Illusion & ECE (Table 3.1), Perceptual Chattering, Temporal Expiration. -->
<!-- covers: Real-World Incident Callout Box for Tesla Autopilot Williston 2016 crash. -->
<!-- covers: The Proposal-Permission Principle Callout Contract. -->
<!-- covers: The Two-Speed Brain Architecture (#fig-two-speed-brain). -->
<!-- covers: Progressive disclosure: explaining why neural networks cannot evaluate their own physical truth. -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
While learned foundation models dismantle the classical wall of generalizability, they introduce what control theorists and safety certifiers consider a profound liability: the complete loss of formal mathematical verifiability.[^fn-math-symbolic-connectionist]

A deep neural network is a high-dimensional, non-linear statistical function. Unlike classical linear or convex controllers, a deep network is generally non-Lipschitz, meaning that infinitesimal perturbations in sensor inputs can induce massive, unpredictable excursions in output actions. An engineer cannot prove Lyapunov stability, cannot guarantee worst-case execution bounds, and cannot achieve formal structural code coverage under ISO 26262. A model that achieves $99.9\%$ empirical success on benchmark datasets will still produce an ungrounded hallucination on the $0.1\%$ distributional tail that can destroy physical hardware or injure human operators.[^fn-math-lipschitz-calibration]

Because a learned brain operates through statistical approximation, its failure modes are fundamentally distinct from traditional software defects. A classical program fails by throwing an exception, hanging in an infinite loop, or crashing. A neural network fails silently by emitting pristine, mathematically bounded tensors that command catastrophic physical motions. Systems architects must design around four primary cognitive vulnerabilities:

### Semantic Hallucinations {.unnumbered}

A semantic hallucination occurs when a model's latent representation generates a plausible prediction that has no physical counterpart in reality. When an autonomous mobile manipulator approaches a workstation in an industrial cleanroom, sunlight reflecting off a polished transparent acrylic safety shield may be processed by the visual transformer as open traversable space. The policy outputs a high-confidence intent lease and trajectory chunk commanding the arm to reach straight through the barrier. The output tensor passes all numerical range checks, but its underlying physical premise is entirely false.

### The Softmax Illusion and Out-of-Distribution Overconfidence {.unnumbered}

Deployment interfaces frequently mistake mathematical normalization for physical probability. In deep neural networks, output logits are passed through a softmax function:

$$p_k = \frac{\exp(z_k)}{\sum_{j=1}^K \exp(z_j)}$$

The resulting values sum to $1.0$ by mathematical definition, not because the model is physically certain. When an embodied machine encounters out-of-distribution (OOD) observations—such as novel optical textures, deep shadows, or lens water droplets—deep networks routinely assign confidence scores exceeding $0.95$ to completely erroneous classifications.

Evaluating the true relationship between reported model confidence and empirical physical success requires measuring **Expected Calibration Error (ECE)**:[^fn-math-ece-formulation]

$$\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} |\text{acc}(B_m) - \text{conf}(B_m)|$$

As detailed in @tbl-03-calibration-degradation, under severe distribution shift, calibration collapses: reported confidence remains high ($\text{conf} > 0.85$) while empirical physical task success drops toward zero ($\text{acc} < 0.10$). Without independent supervisory verification, trusting raw softmax confidence leads directly to physical failure.

| Distribution Shift Regime               | Physical & Environmental Trigger                                             | Reported Conf. vs Measured Acc. ($\text{conf} \text{ vs } \text{acc}$) | Calibration Gap ($\Delta \text{ECE}$)         | Downstream Supervisory Action                                                      |
|:----------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **In-Distribution** (Nominal Baseline)  | Clean optics, structured laboratory lighting, nominal workpiece textures     | $\text{conf}=0.91, \, \text{acc}=0.89$                                 | $\text{ECE} \le 0.035$ (Calibrated)           | Full autonomous execution permitted; nominal velocity profiles                     |
| **Near-OOD Shift** (Covariate Shift)    | Specular reflections, lens water droplets, dynamic shadow transitions        | $\text{conf}=0.89, \, \text{acc}=0.52$                                 | $\Delta \text{ECE} = +0.370$ (Overconfident)  | Selective abstention triggered: clamp velocity, initiate exploratory tactile probe |
| **Far-OOD Shift** (Semantic Shift)      | Uncataloged deformable obstacles, human limb intrusion into workspace        | $\text{conf}=0.78, \, \text{acc}=0.08$                                 | $\Delta \text{ECE} = +0.700$ (Pathological)   | Immediate proposal refusal: hold position, engage controlled braking               |
| **Sensor Degradation** (Hardware Drift) | Photodetector thermal noise ($>75^\circ\text{C}$), focal blur from vibration | $\text{conf}=0.84, \, \text{acc}=0.31$                                 | $\Delta \text{ECE} = +0.530$ (Silent failure) | Trigger operational downgrade; restrict kinematics to certified safety envelope    |

: **Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Failure Profiles across Distribution Shift Regimes.** Breakdown of nominal model confidence versus empirical physical task success rates, calibration error degradation, and deterministic supervisory actions under progressive environmental and sensor anomalies. {#tbl-03-calibration-degradation}

### Perceptual Chattering and Covariate Shift {.unnumbered}

When an agent operates in ambiguous sensory environments, discrete classification heuristics can oscillate rapidly across consecutive time steps. In the 2018 Tempe autonomous vehicle collision [@ntsb2019uber], the perception system reclassified a pedestrian pushing a bicycle multiple times over $5.6\text{ seconds}$ between *vehicle*, *bicycle*, and *unknown*, resetting trajectory path predictions to zero on every discrete state transition.[^fn-inc-uber-tempe] In physical manipulation, perceptual chattering injects high-frequency direction reversals into trajectory planners, commanding destructive torque chatter that exceeds the mechanical slew rate of actuators.

### Temporal Expiration of Intent {.unnumbered}

Because physical reality is continuously dynamic, a cognitive thought is valid only for a finite duration ($\tau_{\text{valid}}$). If a high-level vision-language model requires $300\text{ ms}$ to deliberate, the physical state of moving obstacles, robotic arms, or chemical reactor valves has already evolved by the time the plan is ready. If downstream communication or execution is delayed, acting upon an expired intent lease means commanding the physical body based on an obsolete mental representation of the universe.

::: {.callout-incident title="The 2016 Williston Tesla Autopilot Collision Under Specular Glare"}
On May 7, 2016, near Williston, Florida, a Tesla Model S operating under Autopilot collided with the side of a refrigerated tractor-semitrailer crossing an uncontrolled highway intersection at $74\text{ mph}$ ($33\text{ m/s}$), resulting in a fatal collision [@ntsb2017tesla].[^fn-inc-tesla-williston]

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigation traced how sensory and architectural failures propagated directly into kinetic destruction:

1. **Specular Glare and Vision Segmentation Failure:** The vehicle approached the intersection against a brightly lit midday sky. The high-reflectance white paint on the broad side panel of the crossing semitrailer produced intense specular glare that washed out optical contrast against the sky. The monocular camera's neural perception classifier failed to detect or segment the lateral trailer as a physical obstacle, misinterpreting the brightly illuminated panel as open overhead sky.
2. **Sensor Fusion and Radar False-Positive Suppression:** The forward millimeter-wave radar detected the metallic trailer structure. However, to prevent "phantom braking" chattering from stationary overhead highway signs and overpasses, the sensor fusion logic suppressed radar returns that lacked confirming bounding boxes from the vision pipeline.
3. **Unchecked Proposal Authority:** Because the learned perception system held uninhibited authority over the vehicle's speed controller without independent geometric occupancy verification, the driving policy operated under the false conviction that the path was clear. It maintained full cruise velocity ($74\text{ mph}$), commanding continuous torque to the drive inverters without initiating pre-collision braking or alerting the driver.
4. **Kinetic Energy Propagation:** The vehicle struck the semitrailer at full speed. Because the trailer bed clearance exceeded the vehicle's hood height, the trailer penetrated directly into the passenger cabin, shearing the A-pillars and roof structure. The vehicle traveled $886\text{ ft}$ ($270\text{ m}$) beyond the impact point before coming to rest.

*Systems Engineering Lesson:* A learned neural network cannot certify its own perceptual truth. Under optical degradation (specular glare, high dynamic range, backlighting), statistical vision models fail through silent semantic omission. Unvalidated perception proposals must never exercise uninhibited execution authority over vehicle kinetic energy ($E_k = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 \approx 1.14\text{ MJ}$) without independent, deterministic geometric boundary validation.
:::

### The Architectural Resolution: The Proposal–Permission Principle {.unnumbered}

Physical AI reconciles this fundamental tension by establishing the **Proposal–Permission Principle**: a learned model possesses the capability to propose candidate goals, spatial estimations, and motion trajectories based on statistical pattern matching, but it possesses **zero authority** to grant physical execution permission. All learned outputs are treated as **unprivileged proposals** ($p_t$) that must pass downstream deterministic safety validation before energizing actuators.

This principle organizes the machine into a **Two-Speed Brain Architecture** (@fig-two-speed-brain). At the top tier, high-capacity Vision-Language-Action foundation models perform slow deliberative cognition (System 2) at $1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$, parsing open-world multimodal streams to interpret semantic commands and emit structured intent leases. At the intermediate tier, generative action chunking diffusion policies and trajectory transformers (System 1.5) operate at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$, unrolling high-level intent into continuous candidate motion chunks. At the base reflex tier, hard real-time safety supervisors (System 1) execute deterministically at $1000\text{ Hz}$ on isolated safety silicon,[^fn-hw-safety-silicon] evaluating candidate proposals against physical kinematic invariants and dynamic stopping clearances ($d_{\text{stop}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$). If a proposal is safe, the supervisor grants execution permission ($u_t$); if it threatens collision or mechanical instability, the supervisor rejects the proposal ($\bot$) and executes a deterministic safe stop.

Treating the learned brain as an unprivileged proposal generator guarantees that even when a model hallucinates, suffers out-of-distribution drift, or generates invalid trajectory setpoints, the physical machine remains protected by deterministic physical invariants. When the System 1 supervisor rejects a candidate proposal or executes a safe holding reflex, the architecture engages a closed-loop **Operational Recovery Loop**: the real-time enforcer immediately asserts an asynchronous notification across the shared IPC mailbox, causing the System 2 deliberative model to flush its pending trajectory buffer, refresh its spatial belief map with the current stationary plant state, and re-prompt the policy with the specific refusal reason (e.g., clearance obstacle detected or kinematic boundary reached), preventing deadlock and continuous chattering.

![The two-speed brain architecture and proposal--permission privilege boundary. The systems architecture partitions into an untrusted deliberative cognitive realm (System 2 vision-language model intent proposer at $1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$ and System 1.5 generative trajectory planner at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$) and a trusted hard real-time safety realm (System 1 deterministic barrier enforcer at $1000\text{ Hz}$). All unprivileged candidate proposals ($p_t$, dashed path) must cross the non-negotiable proposal--permission privilege boundary, where deterministic safety monitors validate dynamic stopping clearances and state constraints before granting permission ($u_t$, solid path) to energize physical actuators, falling back to deterministic emergency-stop refusals (rejection) upon any contract violation.](figures/fig03_two_speed_brain.svg){#fig-two-speed-brain fig-pos="t" width=90%}
<!-- END -->

## Systems Stress-Tests {#sec-brain-3-6}

<!-- SECTION 3.6 -->
<!-- claim: Five foundational engineering dilemmas test the balance between learned intelligence and physical reality across the three physical machine archetypes. -->
<!-- covers: 1. Verifiability Dilemma on Factory Floor. 2. Semantic Hallucination under Specular Glare. 3. Uncalibrated Confidence in Precision Contact. 4. Covariate Shift and Perceptual Chattering. 5. The Stale Intent Dilemma across Discrete and Continuous Systems. -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
To evaluate whole-system engineering judgment, consider five foundational dilemmas where the cognitive brain confronts the unyielding realities of the physical world across Mobile Systems, Manipulators, and Process/Energy Systems.

### Stress-Test 1: The Verifiability Dilemma on a Factory Floor {.unnumbered}

*The scenario.* An automotive assembly plant evaluates two competing approaches for installing wiring harnesses into car doors. Approach A uses classical trajectory optimization and explicit CAD models, achieving $100\%$ formal MC/DC safety certification under ISO 26262, but failing on $42\%$ of flexible harness insertions due to unmodeled cable deformations. Approach B uses an end-to-end diffusion policy trained on 5,000 human teleoperation demonstrations, achieving a $96\%$ empirical insertion success rate, but providing zero mathematical proof of worst-case joint velocities or contact forces.

*The systems dilemma.* Plant management cannot deploy Approach A because it stops the production line on nearly half the assembly cycles. However, safety compliance officers refuse to sign off on Approach B because deep neural policies cannot provide formal ISO safety certificates.

*The systems verdict: Architectural partitioning.* Neither pure extreme is viable. The physical AI solution wraps the high-capacity diffusion policy (Approach B) inside a deterministic Control Barrier Function safety shield (Approach A). The learned brain provides the open-world deformable compliance to seat the harness, while the real-time supervisor deterministically clamps actuator current and joint limits to guarantee physical safety.

### Stress-Test 2: Semantic Hallucination under Specular Reflections {.unnumbered}

*The scenario.* An autonomous mobile manipulator in a cleanroom uses a Vision-Language-Action policy to transport chemical reagent vials. While approaching a transfer station, sunlight reflects off a polished transparent acrylic safety barrier. The visual transformer processes the specular glare as empty traversable space, outputting a high-confidence intent lease and trajectory chunk that commands the arm to reach directly through the physical barrier plane.

*The systems dilemma.* The output tensor satisfies all structural checks: coordinates are within mathematical bounds, values contain no NaNs, and the packet arrives within its $40.0\text{ ms}$ deadline. The learned model operates under the statistical conviction that the path is unobstructed. Because semantic truth cannot be determined from neural activations alone, executing the proposal would shatter the acrylic enclosure and destroy the manipulator payload.

*The systems verdict: Semantic opacity invariant.* A neural network cannot certify its own perceptual truth. In an embodied architecture, all learned trajectory proposals must be checked against independent, deterministic geometric boundary models before actuation permission is granted.

### Stress-Test 3: Uncalibrated Confidence in Precision Contact {.unnumbered}

*The scenario.* An articulated six-axis robotic manipulator performs precision bin-picking and placement of machined metal castings. The learned grasping policy outputs candidate end-effector poses accompanied by a predicted success probability $\hat{p} \in [0, 1]$. In an analytical evaluation across 100 grasp attempts where the model reports confidence in the narrow range of $\hat{p} \approx 0.90$, physical execution on the fixture yields 64 successful seating operations and 36 dropped or misaligned parts.

*The systems dilemma.* The system supervisor uses predicted confidence to trigger an abstention policy, delegating low-confidence grasps to an operator or an exploratory tactile scan. The $0.26$ calibration gap between reported confidence ($0.90$) and empirical success ($0.64$) destroys the monotonic probability ranking required for selective execution, passing hazardous proposals downstream to mechanical actuators while providing an illusion of safety.

*The systems verdict: Calibration gating law.* Raw softmax outputs and logit scores represent ungrounded network activation states rather than true physical probabilities. A learned model cannot hold selective authority over mechanical actuators without empirical calibration curves validated across the target operational domain.

### Stress-Test 4: Covariate Shift and Perceptual Chattering {.unnumbered}

*The scenario.* A visual navigation policy on an automated delivery robot encounters a dynamic construction zone where traffic cones are draped with wet reflective tarps. The perception pipeline reclassifies the scene on every $50.0\text{ ms}$ cycle, alternating rapidly between "static obstacle," "movable drape," and "free pathway."

*The systems dilemma.* Discretized categorization heuristics reset motion planning on every classification change, creating severe chattering setpoints that demand instantaneous direction reversals beyond the torque slew limits of the wheel drive motors. The learned brain oscillates in its semantic hypothesis, injecting high-frequency jerk into the physical chassis.

*The systems verdict: Latent continuity invariant.* Physical bodies cannot tolerate discrete cognitive chattering. Robust sensorimotor architectures must use continuous latent representations and multi-step action chunking to maintain kinodynamic trajectory smoothness across ambiguous perceptual states.

### Stress-Test 5: The Stale Intent Dilemma in Continuous Process Operations {.unnumbered}

*The scenario.* A learned optimization policy manages reagent feed rates and cooling flows on a continuous exothermic chemical reactor column. The deliberative model generates an intent lease to increase monomer feed by $12\%$ over a validity window of $\tau_{\text{lease}} = 500\text{ ms}$. Due to thread preemption on the application host, the trajectory chunk reaches the deterministic fieldbus gateway $580\text{ ms}$ after generation ($80\text{ ms}$ past expiration). In the intervening interval, an exothermic thermal pulse elevated core temperature near the thermal runaway threshold ($T_{\text{core}} \to T_{\text{crit}}$).

*The systems dilemma.* The proposed feed rate curve is smooth, numerically valid, and would optimize yield under nominal conditions. However, the intent lease is stale. Applying additional monomer feed under an unmonitored thermal excursion would accelerate exothermic heating beyond the cooling jacket's heat dissipation capacity.

*The systems verdict: Temporal validity invariant.* The real-time safety enforcer evaluates authority and temporal validity, never semantic plausibility. An expired proposal is an invalid proposal; the nervous system must reject late packets deterministically and engage emergency cooling reflux.
<!-- END -->

## Summary {#sec-brain-3-7}

<!-- SECTION 3.7 -->
<!-- claim: Physical AI is the deliberate synthesis of classical guarantees and learned open-world representations. -->
<!-- covers: Master comparison table: Classical vs Learned across 7 core systems axes. -->
<!-- covers: Custom Key Chapter Takeaways callout box. -->
<!-- covers: Direct handoff to Chapter 4 (The Real-Time Nervous System). -->

<!-- BEGIN -->
Physical AI represents neither the blind abandonment of classical control theory nor the uncritical worship of machine learning black boxes. It is the deliberate, principled synthesis of both traditions.

Where an engineering problem is bounded, static, and analytically tractable—such as enforcing joint torque clamps, verifying stopping distances, or solving quadratic programs at $1000\text{ Hz}$—we rely unconditionally on deterministic classical algorithms. Where an engineering problem requires parsing the infinite visual and geometric complexity of the open world—such as open-vocabulary language grounding, deformable object manipulation, and high-dimensional trajectory synthesis—we embrace learned foundation models.

::: {.callout-takeaways}
- **Five Ideal Properties:** Embodied cognition requires semantic generalizability, continuous sensory robustness, metric spatial-temporal grounding, multi-rate cadence decoupling, and bounded execution authority.
- **Why We Learn (The Four Pillars):** Physical AI adopts learned models for open-world generalizability, continuous sensory robustness, complex multi-contact/deformable dynamics, and empirical scaling with compute and demonstrations.
- **The Five Stages of Cognition:** Information flows sequentially through $\text{Ingestion} \to \text{Perception} \to \text{Memory} \to \text{Intent} \to \text{Planning}$. Detailed mathematical formulations are explored in Part III (@sec-perception through @sec-enforcement).
- **Two Cognitive Cadences:** Multi-billion-parameter foundation models operate at slow cadences ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$) for intent reasoning, while **Action Chunking** (ACT / Diffusion Policy) amortizes inference to emit trajectory chunks at $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$.
- **The Proposal–Permission Principle:** The learned brain operates strictly as an **unprivileged proposal engine** ($p_t$), possessing capability to suggest actions, but zero authority to command actuators without deterministic validation.
- **Softmax is Not Probability:** Exponentiated logits sum to one by mathematical definition, not physical truth. Models exhibit severe overconfidence under out-of-distribution shift, requiring empirical calibration (ECE) and selective abstention.
:::

The foundational trade-offs between these paradigms are synthesized in @tbl-03-classical-vs-learned.

| Systems Dimension                 | Classical Analytical Methods                                                                       | Learned Foundation Models                                                                                    | Physical AI Architectural Synthesis                                                   |
|:----------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Foundational Principle**        | Analytical differential equations, geometry, CAD models, Lyapunov stability                        | High-capacity neural representations fitted to empirical multimodal data                                     | **Hybrid Hierarchy:** Learned intent proposals gated by analytical safety shields     |
| **Generalizability & Perception** | **Brittle & Low:** Confined to pre-modeled geometries; fails under novel textures or optical flare | **Unprecedented & Continuous:** Open-vocabulary language grounding; latent manifolds absorb noise            | **Unprivileged Deliberation:** Foundation models synthesize continuous semantic goals |
| **Mathematical Verifiability**    | **Complete:** Formal proofs of stability, MC/DC code coverage, ISO compliance                      | **Zero:** Non-Lipschitz black boxes; no formal worst-case execution proofs                                   | **Proposal–Permission Boundary:** Safety is guaranteed at the deterministic gate      |
| **Temporal Pacing**               | **Hard Real-Time:** Deterministic microsecond execution loops ($1\text{ kHz}$)                     | **Multi-Rate:** Deliberative intent ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$) vs Action Chunking ($20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$) | **Two-Speed Brain:** Action chunks amortize slow deliberative foundation models       |
| **Failure Modes & Fallback**      | Boolean branch crashes; failure on uncataloged objects; rule exhaustion                            | Semantic hallucinations; out-of-distribution overconfidence; cognitive drift                                 | **Deterministic Fallback:** Rejection gates catch invalid proposals and safe-stop     |

: **Master Comparison: Classical Analytical Methods vs. Learned Foundation Models in Physical AI.** Architectural trade-offs across generalizability, sensory robustness, verifiability, pacing, and fallback modes, highlighting the physical AI synthesis that partitions proposal capability from execution authority. {#tbl-03-classical-vs-learned}

These cognitive stages define how an embodied agent perceives, remembers, reasons, and plans. Yet a mental model alone cannot move physical mass. In @sec-nervous, we construct the **Real-Time Nervous System**—the heterogeneous computing platform, shared memory buses, lock-free communication protocols, and deterministic hardware watchdogs that physically bridge the deliberative Brain to the dynamical Body.

[^fn-math-symbolic-connectionist]: **Connectionist vs. Symbolic Duality.** Physical AI unites the statistical learning of connectionist neural networks (used for high-capacity proposal synthesis) with deterministic symbolic logic (used for real-time safety enforcement).

[^fn-arch-curriculum-deepdives]: **Curriculum Architecture.** While this chapter establishes the overarching mental model of embodied cognition, deep algorithmic formulations for each stage are detailed in Part III (@sec-perception through @sec-enforcement).

[^fn-trans-unprivileged-control]: Unprivileged proposal isolates actuators behind deterministic Control Barrier Functions.

[^fn-trans-roofline-ai]: **For AI & Theory Readers:** The Patterson Roofline proves why scaling raw FLOP capacity on edge SoCs cannot increase inference frequency if the memory bus bandwidth $B_{\text{mem}}$ remains the operational bottleneck.

[^fn-trans-vla-concept]: **For MLSys Readers:** A VLA model replaces discrete text tokens with continuous trajectory chunks $\mathbf{a}_{t:t+H}$ commanding joint angles or twists.

[^fn-hw-lpddr5-bandwidth]: **LPDDR5 Memory Subsystem Throughput.** The $204.8\text{ GB/s}$ peak bandwidth on a canonical heterogeneous SoC (256-bit LPDDR5 at $6400\text{ MT/s}$) drops to $70\text{--}75\%$ sustained efficiency ($145\text{ GB/s}$) due to DRAM bank turnaround and auto-refresh ($t_{\text{RFC}}$).

[^fn-math-roofline-derivation]: **Roofline Hardware Ridge Point.** With $P_{\text{peak}} = 275\text{ TFLOP/s}$ and $B_{\text{mem}} = 204.8\text{ GB/s}$, the ridge point is $I_{\text{knee}} = 1342.8\text{ FLOP/byte}$. Single-token generation ($I \approx 1$) achieves $<0.1\%$ peak compute efficiency ($99.9\%$ idle time stalled on DRAM).

[^fn-math-action-chunking]: **Action Chunk Horizon Bounds.** Horizon $H$ balances latency amortization against open-loop state drift $\|\mathbf{e}_{t+H}\| \le \frac{\epsilon_{\text{tot}}}{L_f}(e^{L_f H \Delta t} - 1)$. Setting $H \in [16, 64]$ yields stable $320\text{--}1280\text{ ms}$ windows.

[^fn-math-lipschitz-calibration]: **Non-Lipschitz Neural Mappings.** Deep ReLU/GELU networks exhibit global Lipschitz constants $L$ that scale exponentially with depth ($\prod \|W_l\|$). Infinitesimal sensor perturbations can induce massive trajectory jumps without pointwise safety guarantees.

[^fn-std-ece-ul4600]: Under ANSI/UL 4600 §8.4, uncalibrated neural confidence ($\text{ECE} > 0.05$) cannot serve as an ASIL safety gate.

[^fn-inc-uber-tempe]: NTSB report [@ntsb2019uber]: semantic classification toggling repeatedly reset tracking histories before impact.

[^fn-inc-tesla-williston]: NTSB report [@ntsb2017tesla]: monocular vision failed on trailer glare against a bright sky.

[^fn-hw-safety-silicon]: Invariant violations force PWMs to Hi-Z in $<100\text{ ns}$ (Safe Torque Off).
